previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old female was admitted for increased total body edema and concern for possible cellulitis in the left lower extremity. The swelling was attributed to chronic lymphedema, venous insufficiency, and obesity, with no evidence of heart failure, kidney injury, or liver disease. A low-dose Lasix trial improved facial and hand swelling, but the medication was not continued at discharge due to prior renal risks. Persistent erythema in the left leg prompted a short course of clindamycin. Her INR remained therapeutic on warfarin, phenytoin levels were normal, and sleep apnea was noted for outpatient follow-up. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to elevate her legs, wear compression stockings, and follow up with her primary care provider regarding diuretic management and further evaluation.

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient is a ___ woman with a history of DVT/PE (on 
Coumadin), obesity, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, OSA, h/o 
DVT/PE (on Coumadin), hypothyroidism, seizure disorder (on 
phenytoin), and recurrent lower extremity cellulitis presenting 
with right lower extremity cellulitis.  

# RLE cellulitis: Pt presented with erythema, pain, and 
increased swelling in the right leg.  Ultrasound was negative 
for DVT in the right leg.  She was started on IV vancomycin with 
improvement in area of erythema and pain.  PICC line was placed. 
Vancomycin trough was elevated at 31.8 during hospital stay; she 
was discharged with home ___ services for continued IV 
vancomycin (at a lower dose) for a total course of ten days.  
She should have a trough drawn before her third dose of the 
reduced dose.  She was continued on her home regimen of 
oxycodone and morphine for her pain with good relief.  
  
# History of DVT/PE: Per patient, PE was in ___ and she had a 
UE DVT ___ years ago. Pt was on lifelong anticoagulation with 
coumadin; however on admission, INR was subtherapeutic at 1.1. 
RLE ultrasound was negative for any DVT in right leg.  RUE 
ultrasound was also negative for DVT (see below).  She was 
placed on increased dose of coumadin and for home ___ services 
to recheck INR.   She was also placed on SC heparin for DVT 
prophylaxis as INR was subtherapeutic. INR was 1.2 by time of 
discharge.
  
# RUE swelling: Pt with RUE swelling and pain where initial PIV 
was. This was likely due to IV infiltration.  Given significant 
history of VTE, ultrasound was performed which was negative for 
DVT. She was treated symptomatically with warm compresses and 
elevation with improvement in the swelling by time of discharge. 

  
# Anasarca: Per PCP, it was becoming increasingly difficult to 
diuresis pt at home and pt had increasing anasarca.  It was 
recommended that pt be discharged to rehab both for additional 
diuresis as well as continued IV antibiotic therapy for her 
cellulitis.  However, pt refused rehab.  She was diuresed with 
40mg IV lasix during hospital stay along with her po metolazone 
with good urine output.  Her home lisinopril was decreased to 
allow for further diuresis as BPs were low normal.  She was 
discharged on 60mg po lasix in addition to her metolazone. She 
should have electrolytes rechecked with her ___.   
  
# Urinary frequency:  Pt reported increased urinary frequency, 
most likely from her increased dose of diuretics.  Urine culture 
was negative for UTI. 
  
# Hypertension: BPs were low normal in systolic 100s-110s during 
hospital stay.  Because of need for further diuresis, pt's home 
lisinopril was reduced to 5mg daily.
  
# Hyperlipidemia: She was continued on her home Zetia.  
  
# Seizure disorder: Patient was on phenytoin to prevent 
seizures. Phenytoin dose was 14.8.  She was continued on home 
dose of phenytoin during hospital stay.
  
# GERD: She was continued on PPI during hospital stay. 
  
# Hypothyroidism: She was continued on home levothyroxine 
therapy.
